reason: No change was needed: the story diff only adds a PR check note about which claim types the policy accepts. The plan still has one happy end-to-end lifecycle case with a webhooks token, one happy case for the WebhookClient app, one case per endpoint where a basket-only token is refused (GET list, GET by id, POST, DELETE), and one anonymous 401 case, all on the test stack.

items.title: A webhooks-scoped token can create, list, read and delete alice's subscription
covers: Expected: a token with the webhooks scope keeps working as it does today
Endpoints GET, GET by id, POST, DELETE
items.reason: The fix adds a scope requirement to the whole `/api/webhooks` group; if the policy misreads the `scope` claim of a real Identity token (for example because the JWT handler maps the claim type), every legitimate caller is locked out. Only the test stack issues a real JWT, so this regression runs at the e2e layer through the API.

items.title: WebhookClient app registers a webhook and lists it after alice signs in
covers: Expected: the token the webhooks client app gets when a user signs in keeps working
items.reason: The ticket names the WebhookClient app's sign-in token (client `webhooksclient`, code flow, scopes `openid webhooks`) as the one that must keep working. It is a different client and flow from TC-01's, and it is only reachable through the WebhookClient UI on the test stack, so this case is e2e through the browser.

items.title: Basket-only token is refused on GET /api/webhooks and lists nothing
covers: Expected: token without the webhooks scope refused; no subscription listed
items.reason: This is reproduction step 2 of the bug: a token issued for Basket.API listed alice's subscriptions. It needs a real `basketswaggerui` token from Identity.API, so it runs on the test stack.

items.title: Basket-only token is refused on GET /api/webhooks/{id}
covers: Expected: refused on every Webhooks.API endpoint (GET by id)
items.reason: The ticket requires refusal on every endpoint, and reading a single subscription exposes the same data as the list. A separate case catches a fix applied to the list route only. Real tokens require the test stack.

items.title: Basket-only token is refused on POST /api/webhooks and nothing is created
covers: Expected: refused on every endpoint; no subscription created
items.reason: The bug report says a basket token could register subscriptions; registering a webhook lets the holder receive alice's order data at a URL of their choice. The case also checks persistence, so a refusal that still wrote a row is caught. Real tokens require the test stack.

items.title: Basket-only token is refused on DELETE /api/webhooks/{id} and the subscription survives
items.reason: This is reproduction step 3: the basket token deleted alice's subscription. Asserting that the subscription still exists afterwards proves no delete happened, not only that the status changed. Real tokens require the test stack.

items.title: Request without a token is refused with 401
covers: Expected: requests without a webhooks-scoped token are refused (no token at all)
items.reason: Replacing the group's plain authorization requirement with a scope policy could drop the authenticated-user requirement; a request with no token at all must still be refused. It runs on the stack next to the other cases, against the real JWT bearer setup.

subject: test-planner
reason: Every endpoint (GET list, GET by id, POST, DELETE) has a basket-token refusal case with persistence checks, both repro steps map to cases, and both the API webhooks-scoped token and the WebhookClient sign-in token are covered as regressions, with concrete steps verified against the code. One point off: TC-03..06 require exactly 403 when the story accepts 401 or 403. Question for the story author: should a token carrying both basket and webhooks scopes be accepted?

items.reason: TC-03 to TC-06 require exactly 403 Forbidden, but the story's Expected section accepts 401 or 403 for a token without the webhooks scope. A fix that meets the ticket by returning 401 would fail these cases. Assert that the status is 401 or 403, or state that 403 comes from the Implementation Notes decision and is not a ticket requirement. The plan already lists this under Open questions.

subject: test-automation
reason: All seven cases are implemented faithfully on the test stack with real Identity tokens obtained as _index.md specifies (scope claims verified); each step's status and body expectations, including must-not-happen checks (no Location, [] after refused POST, subscription survives refused DELETE, no leaked data), are asserted with exact values; TC-02 keyframes show alice signed in, the default token kept and exactly one registered row with the expected destination and token.

subject: test-automation
reason: All seven cases are implemented faithfully at the e2e layer. Each test uses real Identity-issued implicit-flow tokens, and the beforeAll checks that their scope claims are exactly ['webhooks'] and ['basket']. Every expected status and body item is asserted with exact values, including the negative ones: no Location header, the body does not contain DEST_URL or 'secret', and the subscription survives the refused DELETE. The beforeEach empties alice's subscriptions so each case starts from []. The TC-BUG-31-02 keyframes show alice signed in, the default token on /add-webhook, and exactly one grid row with the expected Destination and Token and no error. The token helper matches the neighbouring bug-15, bug-16 and bug-30 specs, and scenario bug-31 exists.
